title: Neznaika's Adventures
author: Nikolai Nosov
short_summary: In Flower City live the shorties, each about the size of a small cucumber, and every one of them has a name that says exactly what they do: Znayka knows everything, Pilyulkin doctors, Vintik and Shpuntik mend things, Tyubik paints. And then there is Neznaika, who knows nothing and will not learn — but does wear canary-yellow trousers, an orange shirt, a green tie and a wide blue hat. When Znayka builds a hot-air balloon, the whole company sets off on a journey that ends nowhere near where it was meant to.
extended_summary:
The shorties of Flower City are about as tall as a small cucumber, and each one is named for what he does: Znayka is the scholar in the black suit and spectacles, Pilyulkin is the doctor, Vintik and Shpuntik are the mechanics, Tyubik paints, Guslya plays music, Ponchik eats and Siropchik drinks fizzy syrup. And there is Neznaika, who knows nothing and has no intention of learning, but who dresses so brightly that everyone says he has got himself up like a parrot.

Neznaika tries in turn to be a musician, an artist and a poet. He picks his instrument by how loud it is, paints portraits that his sitters demand be taken down, and writes verses his friends refuse to listen to. Each time he drops the whole business the moment it stops going well immediately.

Then Znayka has the idea of building a hot-air balloon, and after a long construction the shorties set off. The air in the envelope cools, the balloon comes down, and the company lands in the Green City, where only girl shorties live. Neznaika is found first and taken to Sineglazka's house — and promptly announces that he built the balloon himself and rescued everybody. The others are carried off by the strict doctor Medunitsa. When Znayka appears, the whole story collapses, but Neznaika is forgiven. At the farewell ball the shorties grow homesick and go back to Flower City — and Neznaika, for the first time, sits down to learn something.

questions.prompt: How big are the shorties of Flower City?

options: About the size of a small cucumber
About the size of a full-grown cat
As tall as a seven-year-old child
No bigger than a single pea

questions.explanation: Nosov fixes the scale on the first page and then never breaks it: hence the Cucumber River, a burdock leaf for a tree, and a hot-air balloon about the size of a real watermelon. Half the pleasure of the book is that its world is measured in vegetables.

questions.prompt: Why is Neznaika called by that name?

options: He knows nothing and will not learn anything
He never knows the way home and keeps getting lost
He can never remember anybody else's name
He did not know his own name when he arrived

questions.explanation: In Flower City a name is a job: Znayka knows, Pilyulkin doctors, Tyubik paints. Neznaika's name is built the same honest way, and it describes not only what he cannot do but the fact that he will not set about learning.

questions.prompt: Neznaika wears canary-yellow trousers, an orange shirt, a green tie and a blue hat, and people say he has dressed himself up like a ___.
questions.explanation: Nosov dresses him louder and sillier than anyone else, and it is not only a joke. Neznaika needs to be looked at, and the whole plot turns on the same thing: he lies about the balloon not for profit but to be watched.

questions.prompt: Whose idea is it to build the hot-air balloon?

options: Znayka's
Vintik and Shpuntik's
Neznaika's
Tyubik's

questions.explanation: Znayka thinks of it, the whole town builds it, and the credit is taken by the one who did nothing. Nosov sets this up very carefully: the reader has watched who worked, which is exactly why Neznaika's boasting in the Green City is so infuriating.

questions.prompt: Put the events of the journey in the order they happen.

items: Znayka has the idea of building a balloon
The whole town works on building it
The balloon rises and the journey begins
The air in the envelope cools and it comes down
Neznaika announces that he built it and saved everyone
Znayka appears and the whole story collapses

questions.explanation: Notice where the lie sits in the chain: not at the start and not at the end, but exactly between the landing and Znayka's arrival. Neznaika gets about half a book of somebody else's glory — which is what makes the exposure so uncomfortable.

questions.prompt: Match each shorty to what they do.

right: The scholar in the black suit and spectacles

questions.explanation: Each name is also a description, and Nosov never once breaks his own rule. That is why it is funny: in a town where your name states your skill, there lives a shorty whose name states the absence of any.

questions.prompt: Sort each detail by which of the two towns it belongs to.

options.label: A whole street working on a balloon
Boy and girl shorties living together
The home Neznaika and his friends come from
A town where only girl shorties live
A strict doctor putting them all in hospital

questions.explanation: The second town is not just a new place but a mirror: the same occupations, different inhabitants, different rules — and the visiting boys are treated as hooligans on arrival. Medunitsa treats them for things they have not got, which is an error of exactly the same size as Neznaika's about her.

questions.prompt: Why does Neznaika tell the girls that he built the balloon?

options: He is found alone, and there is nobody to contradict him
He is afraid of being sent straight back home again
He wants to draw attention away from his injured friends
Znayka told him to say it before they ever took off

questions.explanation: He arrives in the town by himself, people listen, and after that it is hard to stop: one invention needs the next. Nosov prices the lie very precisely — not a punishment, but having to look everyone in the face at once when Znayka walks in.

questions.prompt: Neznaika took credit for other people's work and boasted about it to a whole town, and when he was found out he was forgiven. Was it right to forgive him, or should there have been some punishment? Give your reasons.
questions.explanation: Both positions can earn full marks. A strong 'right to forgive' answer notices that nobody was seriously harmed and that afterwards Neznaika sits down to learn for the first time in his life. A strong 'should have been punished' answer notices that he claimed the work of friends who were in hospital at the time, and that embarrassment alone is a light price. Accept either, argued from the book.

questions.prompt: In Flower City a name tells you everything: Znayka knows, Pilyulkin doctors, Vintik mends. Invent a new shorty: what is their name, what do they do, and how does the name fit the work?
questions.explanation: There is no single right answer. A strong answer invents a name that explains the occupation by itself — built, as Nosov's are, from a word for the job or the habit — and says briefly what this shorty does all day. A name with no connection to the work has missed the joke the whole book runs on.

questions.prompt: In the Green City, Neznaika is found first and taken to the house of a girl shorty called ___.
questions.explanation: She is the one he tells his great invention to. Her name follows a different rule from the others in the book — it describes how she looks rather than what she does, and the Green City is the only place where the naming works that way.

questions.prompt: Why do the shorties eventually go back to Flower City?

options: They start to feel homesick
The girls throw them out for bad behaviour
Znayka finds a way to repair the balloon
The Green City runs out of food for them all

questions.explanation: Not a quarrel and not a disaster — plain homesickness, at the farewell ball. Nosov ends the adventure quietly and puts everyone back where they started; the only thing in the book that has changed is Neznaika, who finally sits down to study.
